text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of high uric acid levels or previous gout attacks, and does the pain in your left great toe ever become acutely red, hot, and swollen? I also need to know if you have noticed any joint stiffness in the morning, and if so, how long does it last?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given that your pain worsens with activity and improves with rest, this pattern strongly suggests osteoarthritis rather than inflammatory arthritis or gout. I will proceed to confirm this by requesting imaging of your affected joints. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of Knees and Hips

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-Ray of Knees and Hips: Findings show joint space narrowing with osteophyte formation, suggestive of osteoarthritis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging results confirm osteoarthritis, which aligns perfectly with your symptoms of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest. I have enough information to make a final determination. DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis
